prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” — the right interior painter depends on your needs (residential vs. commercial), budget, timeline, scope (one room vs whole home), and aesthetic priorities. I can help you find the best fit. To get started, please tell me:
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood in St. Louis
- Residential or commercial job
- How many rooms / approximate square footage
- Desired start date and budget range (if any)

Meanwhile, here’s a short guide you can use right away to identify top interior painters in St. Louis and choose the best one:

How to find top local painters
- Search local reviews: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and BBB. Look for 4.5+ average and lots of recent reviews.
- Get referrals: Ask neighbors, local Facebook groups, Nextdoor, or your real estate agent.
- Check credentials: Confirm the contractor has liability insurance and, if required, any local licensing or registration.
- Look at portfolios: Ask for before/after photos of similar interior jobs, and request references from recent customers.

Questions to ask every painter
1. Are you licensed and insured? (Get proof.)
2. Do you provide a written estimate with itemized costs (labor, paint, materials)?
3. What brands/quality of paint do you use and what sheen is recommended?
4. How many coats are included? Is priming included if needed?
5. What prep work is included (patching, sanding, caulking, masking)?
6. What is the cleanup policy and project schedule?
7. Do you offer a warranty or touch-up guarantee?
8. Can you provide references and photos of completed interior projects?

Typical pricing (ballpark)
- Per room: $300–$1,200 (small bedroom to large living room) depending on prep and trim work.
- Per sq. ft.: roughly $1.50–$4.00 per sq. ft. for walls and ceilings (varies with paint quality, number of coats, and complexity).
Get 3 written bids to compare.

If you want, I can:
- Pull together a short list of highly rated interior painters near you (tell me ZIP),
- Draft an email/message you can send to painters asking the right questions,
- Or help compare 3 estimates you receive.

Which would you like to do next?
